NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute By Stefanie Waldek Published October 1, 2026 On October 4, Saturn will put on its best show of 2026 as it reaches opposition, appearing brighter and larger in the night sky than at any other point this year. This year will be especially exciting for stargazers: in 2025, Saturn’s rings all but disappeared from view, but this year, they’re back. The event doesn’t last only one night. Because Saturn is so far away from Earth and thus appears to move slowly, the planet will remain a rewarding target for weeks around opposition, giving skywatchers some leeway if clouds spoil the view. Here’s what the alignment means—and what you’ll need to see Saturn and its rings for yourself. What Does Saturn at Opposition Mean? Opposition occurs when Earth passes between the sun and an outer planet, placing that planet directly opposite the sun in our sky. Saturn reaches opposition every 378 days. “This means that we can fully see the side of Saturn that is illuminated by the sun. An island nation in the Mediterranean’s eastern fringes, Cyprus sits at the intersection of three continents — a geographical position that’s profoundly shaped its history. Annexed by an endless parade of empires — including the Greeks, Romans, Byzantines and Ottomans — in 1878, Cyprus became a British protectorate. These last rulers chose the lofty, leafy Troodos Mountains as their summer capital to escape the heat of the coast, and it’s still favoured by locals from spring to autumn. Cyprus became independent in 1960, but vestiges of its storied past are everywhere, from its ancestral grapes, mavro and xynisteri, to mural-washed churches hidden among the hills and turn-of-the-century mansions left by long-gone grandees. Scattered as if on a pirate’s map off England’s southwesterly tip, the Isles of Scilly aren’t a place you stumble over. Travellers need to have booked well ahead for the short, spectacularly scenic transfer by twin-prop plane or helicopter from Penzance to the 140-strong archipelago. Or embark on a three-hour, dolphin-flanked ferry, which plies azure waters towards show-off shelves of pristine white sand. It’s a pilgrimage richly rewarded by a landscape of palms, lipstick-pink sea thrift and sky-blue agapanthus flowers, framing sand-blown, barely-there roads. Beyond St Mary’s, the largest and most populous isle, there are few cars on the four other inhabited outposts of Tresco, Bryher, St Martin’s and St Agnes. They offer a daily invitation to hike and island-hop, with dockings dictated by the tides, and crossings taking mere minutes on jetboat ferries with names like Firethorn and Thunder. Explore Edmonton By Brendan Sainsbury Published May 12, 2026 Nature’s most spectacular light show, the Aurora Borealis, will be even more dazzling this year. This is thanks to a phenomenon called the ‘solar maximum’, defined as the ‘peak’ of the sun’s activity over its 11-year cycle. One of the best places to take advantage of this astronomical event is in Edmonton — North America’s most northerly city, set at latitude of 53.5ºN. With a landscape of wide-open plains, Edmonton and the surrounding region offers a front-row seat to the wonders of the galaxy. Here’s how to spot the auroras using Alberta’s capital as your base. When should I go? Though the solar maximum technically occurred in 2024, this high period of solar activity is expected to continue well into 2026. Put simply, this means that the sun will be sending more electrically charged particles to Earth than usual. Drawing visitors since the 1700s, North Norfolk has long been a place of escapism. You arrive ready to fill your lungs with sea air and let your gaze drift to the horizon. The natural beauty here is not the kind that smacks you in the face and overwhelms with superlatives. The expansive beaches, endless skies, fenland and watery network of the Broads are a more subtle tonic for the soul — you don’t have to work too hard to forget life beyond this somewhat overlooked patch of East Anglia. It’s also a place to get closer to wildlife. Many of the salt marshes in Norfolk offer some of Britain’s best birdwatching, while seals love to sunbathe on the shingle spits at Blakeney Point. Plus, there’s bluebell and snowbell carpets in spring, dragonflies buzzing over lavender fields in summer and woodland ablaze in ochre, yellow and red in autumn. Add it all together and you have a region that promises the kind of serenity many search far and wide for, yet few expect to find so close to home. Fomalhaut, one of the brightest stars in the autumn night sky, lies about 25 light-years from Earth. Roughly 15 times as luminous as our sun, the star is surrounded by vast belts of dust that may hold clues to planets astronomers have yet to discover. NASA, ESA, and the Digitized Sky Survey 2 By Stefanie Waldek Published October 23, 2026 On an autumn night in the Northern Hemisphere, Fomalhaut appears as a bright pinprick in a field of darkness, far from other bright stars. But the star’s apparent solitude is only part of its story: It sits at the center of an expansive system of dusty belts that may hold clues to worlds we have yet to find. The agency drafts its own documents, called guidances, that provide the FDA’s current thinking on how best to comply with laws and regulations governing food, feed and other FDA-regulated products. But food industry associations also draft guidance documents to capture the best practices to produce food, feed and other regulated products in a way that meets federal safety standards. For example, food industry associations may want to draft guidance documents to help their members comply with new requirements under the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA). The National Weather Service office for the San Francisco Bay Area warned that surf up to 35ft (11 meters) was possible, along with dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves. “Stay out of the water, stay off rocks and jetties, and never turn your back on the ocean!” the weather service said on social media . Surfers weren’t deterred, taking advantage of giant waves at the famous Mavericks beach near Half Moon Bay. pages.description: John Holmes and his wife explain why they have returned to Ukraine after initially fleeing.
pages.text: Hull man and wife who fled Ukraine return to a warzone Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live 'Friends think we're idiots for returning to Ukraine' 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kevin Shoesmith East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire John Holmes Liliya Holmes and her British husband John pictured in Odesa, Ukraine When Russian forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, John Holmes – a British national – and his Ukrainian wife Liliya fled the port city of Odesa, fearing for their lives. But after four years in the UK, the draw of home has proven too strong and they have returned to Ukraine's third largest city, undeterred by the sustained threat of air raids. "Friends of ours thought we were idiots for going back to Ukraine," reflects John, 74. "But returning is something we felt we needed to do. "Yes, it's dangerous. Yes, there are drones flying overhead. Yes, you can hear the explosions. But you just have to get on with life as best you can. "Home is Ukraine." During their time away, the pair sought sanctuary in Hull , East Yorkshire, where John was born and raised and has a property. He met Liliya, 64, in Ukraine and had been living there for 30 years until the invasion. "We had built a good life here," he says. Human factors analysis can be used to advance our understanding of the true nature of errors in complex work settings. Research in this area has identified factors that contribute to inefficiencies and quantified the effects of human and organizational factors on performance of critical tasks. The forensic science community can benefit from the application of the substantial body of human factors work to reduce the likelihood and consequences of human error in the scientific interpretation of evidence. To assist the forensic community in this effort, the National Institute of Justice (NIJ) and the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s Special Programs Office partnered to develop a series of expert panels to examine human factors in forensic analyses and develop practices to reduce the likelihood of error based on scientific research. Immunization Information Systems Resources Mar. 30, 2026 About Immunization information systems (IIS) are confidential, population-based, computerized databases that record all immunization doses administered by participating providers to persons residing within a given geopolitical area. What is IIS ? At the point of clinical care, an IIS can provide consolidated immunization histories for use by a vaccination provider in determining appropriate client vaccinations. At the population level, an IIS provides aggregate data on vaccinations for use in surveillance and program operations, and in guiding public health action with the goals of improving vaccination rates and reducing vaccine-preventable disease. Program Support IIS help immunization programs identify populations at high risk for vaccine-preventable diseases and target interventions and resources efficiently. pages.description: For deep reef divers, descending into the ocean’s mesophotic layer can feel like exploring the moon. Discovering never-before-seen marine species is part of the mission.
pages.text: In the ocean's 'twilight zone,' divers risk their lives in search of mysteries | National Geographic By Annie Roth Published December 16, 2025 Agat Bay, Guam — The sun shimmers across the glassy surface of Blue Hole, a heart-shaped underwater sinkhole, as two divers prepare to descend into its treacherous, turquoise abyss. Sounds of buckles clicking, straps tightening, and gases swishing through tubes and tanks fill the tiny boat they’re aboard. The divers—Luiz Rocha, a National Geographic Explorer and an ichthyologist and marine biologist from the California Academy of Sciences, and Mauritius Bell , the academy’s dive safety officer—are gearing up to head 330 feet below the surface, far beyond the reach of most scuba divers. In this part of the ocean, known as the mesophotic or upper “twilight zone,” sunlight is scarce and mysteries abound. Coral reefs thrive in the darkness, harboring life that often appears otherworldly. The researchers suspect this orange fish may be a new species of cardinalfish, likely belonging to the genus Apogonichthyoides. They say they will need further analysis to confirm their hunch. Podría ser una infección de oído. Algunas infecciones de oído, en particular algunas infecciones del oído medio, necesitan tratamiento con antibióticos, pero muchas pueden mejorar sin antibióticos. Hable con el proveedor de atención médica de su hijo/a acerca de cuál es el mejor tratamiento. Información general Los niños tienen más probabilidades que los adultos de contraer infecciones de oído. Existen distintos tipos de infecciones de oído. La infección del oído medio (otitis media aguda) es una infección en el oído medio. La otitis media exudativa es otra condición médica que afecta el oído medio. Esta ocurre cuando se acumula líquido en el oído medio sin causar una infección. No causa fiebre, dolor de oído ni acumulación de pus en el oído medio. El oído de nadador es una infección en el canal auditivo externo. Es distinto de una infección del oído medio. Podría tener una infección urinaria (IU). Los antibióticos tratan las infecciones urinarias. Su proveedor de atención médica puede determinar si tiene una infección urinaria y qué antibiótico necesita. Información general El aparato urinario incluye la vejiga, la uretra y los riñones (ver figura). Las infecciones urinarias son infecciones comunes que ocurren cuando entran bacterias a la uretra, generalmente de la piel o el recto, e infectan el aparato urinario. Aparato urinario de la mujer, incluidas la vejiga y la uretra. Esta imagen muestra cómo las bacterias en la piel o el recto pueden subir por la uretra y causar una infección de vejiga. UU. Estos viajeros deben hacer planes para permanecer fuera de los Estados Unidos al menos por 21 días después de salir de la República Democrática del Congo.
